q: Where and How might the 39 aspirational policy recommendations of the Grand Bargain Project from the Center for Collaborative Democracy contribute to restoring a Healthy Democracy
a: The dataset can't score the Grand Bargain Project — 39 recommendations aren't in GSoD, and the three columns they'd most plainly touch (cross-party cooperation 38, shared factual public sphere 45, economic equality 47) are illustrative or post-2023 only, so treat this as mapping, not measurement. What you see is the one hard number underneath that whole proposal: effective parliament sat in a 75-to-78 band for 42 straight years — 77 at your 25th reunion in 1997, still 78 in 2016 — then fell to 69, 65, 63, 62 from 2017 to 2020 and sits at 60 today, its 50-year low. A project built on forcing negotiated package deals aims at exactly that cliff, plus the two lowest bars on the board, which is either excellent targeting or the civic equivalent of noticing the house is on fire from inside it. Worth saying plainly: the measured series stops in 2020, so nothing here tests whether any of it works — it only tells you where the hole is.
